chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated to us; he said: Some of our companions narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'mar ibn Khallad, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying:
Do men think that they will be left alone on saying, 'We believe,' and not be tried?

Then he asked me: 'What is the trial (fitnah)?' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, we hold that the trial is in religion.' He said: 'They are tried as gold is tried.' Then he said: 'They are purified as gold is purified.'

key_terms.الْفِتْنَةُ: Trial, test, or sedition; here referring to religious testing

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of fitnah in the context of religious testing according to Imam Ali (as)?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Hassan al-Askari (as) elucidates the nature of the 'fitnah' mentioned in Surah Al-Imran, defining it specifically as a rigorous religious trial akin to the smelting of gold. This metaphor underscores the Shia theological concept that true faith is validated and purified through adversity, distinguishing genuine believers from those with superficial conviction during the era of the Minor and Major Disappearance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (2) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob al-Kulayni narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Muhammad that Ma’mar bin Khallad had said: I heard Abul Hasan (Imam Ali) (as) reciting, “Alif Lam Mim.
Do men think that they will be left alone on saying, We believe, and not be tried (with sedition)?”
and then he asked: What is sedition?” I said: “May I die for you! We think that sedition is in religion.” He said: “People are tried as gold is tried. They are purified as gold is purified.”
